notes: Each Opta's USB-C port goes by a USB-C cable to the computer running PLC IDE (as in the diagram), and its ETH RJ-45 port goes by an RJ-45 cable to the Ethernet switch.

The checker flagged the joined edges between an RJ-45 cable end (lead) and the Opta ETH port (kind socket). I misread which edges these were last time and changed the electrical ones instead. The catalogue gives the Opta's ETH port a kind that does not pair with a lead, and I can't change a catalogue port. The cable really does plug into the Opta's RJ-45 socket, so I kept the joined edge but named no port on the Opta side. The electrical edges name the ETH port and were not flagged.
The Ethernet switch is the recommended set-up; without it a single RJ-45 cable could join the two Opta devices directly.
The optional 'Modbus TCP Compatible Device' box in the diagram is omitted because it is not in the parts list.
usb-cable has no ports in the catalogue, so USB edges use null for the cable's port.
The computer is not in the hardware list; it is kept because the USB-C cables need an endpoint and the diagram shows it.
